chapter: Regal Theatre and the changing music scene
title: George Kirby's rise from dishwasher at the DeLisa
summary: Kirby imitated people in the basement; Mike put him on stage with Leon Washington's arrangements and he never looked back.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah, musicians and entertainers also, you get in on the beginning of that career, and you just see them go on.
It's like, I mentioned George Kirby as a performer. He was a dishwasher there in the Club DeLisa, and I saw him go --
Well, did he do occasional spots on the show?

No, what he actually did was, he went through the basement there where the dressing rooms were, and he was always imitating somebody. And so, Mike said, 'we'll put him on the stage, we'll put him on the stage. We'll get together with the Red there, we'll put him on the stage.' So Leon wrote the arrangements for him, we rehearsed him and everything. He never looked back then. Yeah, he just went on.
He does the best imitation of Count Basie.
